grand_strategy.reading:
Somalia is a state whose survival is contracted out. The federal government in Mogadishu
holds a capital, and little else it can call its own; its army is trained and its air power
flown by foreigners, its soldiers' allowances are paid by Brussels and the AU when they are
paid at all, and its budget rests on an IMF programme and a diaspora. A dozen patrons each
buy a piece - Ankara the base, the oil and the space range, Cairo and Asmara a pact aimed at
Addis Ababa, Doha and Riyadh a bet against Abu Dhabi, Beijing a vote against Taipei and
Hargeisa, Washington an air campaign it will not fully fund - and none of them buys the state,
so the patrons' quarrels become Somali politics. Luttwak's logic bites twice. Abroad, the
manoeuvre is relational: Mogadishu has learnt to sit at the seams of its patrons (at El Alamein
on 4 October, then on the telephone to Abiy on the 5th), but the seams run through its own
territory. At home the logic is paradoxical: every step to centralise (the March 2026
amendments, one person one vote, the parallel Gedo administration) makes the federation
weaker, because Puntland, Jubaland and Southwest answer by leaving, and the second week of
October 2026 shows the bill - Hees to al-Shabaab, Balad Hawo to Jubaland, Qansax Dheere to
Laftagareen, troops massed against opposition leaders at home. Three signals that are not rows:
a report, not confirmed by either government, that Somalia will buy Pakistani JF-17 fighters
(14 Oct); a former US ambassador calling the government 'illegitimate' (13 Oct), which is not
Washington's position; and the gap between 1,091 Egyptian AUSSOM troops and the 'about 15,000'
that The National attributes to Egypt in Somalia, which would mean a bilateral deployment outside
AUSSOM that no one has yet documented. The decisive date is 31 December 2026: if UNSOS lapses,
AUSSOM's contributors go home and the patrons' bets are exposed; if the US relents or the Gulf
pays, the same patrons will have bought the next piece.

grand_strategy.reading:
Serbia runs a hedging strategy with one fixed point - Kosovo - and everything else
negotiable. In Luttwak's terms the paradox is structural: the instrument that
protects the fixed point (Russian and Chinese cover at the UN) is the one that
blocks the declared strategic goal (EU membership), and the "neutrality" that
justifies the hedge is financed by the side the hedge is meant to keep at a
distance. Through 2025-26 the hedge stopped paying: the US sanctioned NIS, Russia
refused a long-term gas contract and accused Belgrade over ammunition, the EU
froze funds and talks after the Mladić funeral. Two signals worth watching that
are not rows: Vučić did not attend the 2026 Moscow parade, and in May 2026 Serbia
held its first-ever exercise with NATO on its own soil. The 25 Oct 2026 election
decides whether the strategy has an author at all.

grand_strategy.reading:
Republika Srpska is an entity of a state that it works to hollow out, run by a
party that kept the entity three times in a year in which its leader lost his
office. Its grand strategy is the strategy of a sub-state actor whose
patron needs it loud but not detached: Belgrade wants a Republika Srpska strong
enough to hold Bosnia hostage to the Serbian cause and keep the Sarajevo
state weak, but not so detached that Serbia must either own a secession or
disown a kin. That makes the entity's best move the threat, not the act - and
here Luttwak's paradoxical logic bites hardest. Each time Banja Luka has
crossed the line (the laws of 27 Feb 2025) the state's institutions have
reacted (court annulment, EUFOR reserve troops, entry bans, the High
Representative's funding cut), and those institutions came out stronger and
better tested than before; the repeal of 18 Oct 2025 was a retreat that
Washington rewarded within eleven days. The lesson Banja Luka drew is not
restraint but timing: escalate, absorb, retreat for a price, and let paid
lobbyists and a weaker OHR (Schmidt out in May 2026, an acting High
Representative from 1 July) do the rest.

Signals that are not rows. The plea agreement and the pardon: no source reached
shows a plea agreement between Dodik and the State Prosecutor's Office, and
the prison term was converted into a fine of about EUR 18,660 on 12 Aug 2025
at the defence's request, the six-year ban untouched; in October 2026
Bosnian media discuss whether the state Presidency could pardon him, which
would need all three members and the prior opinion of the State Court - a
debate, not an act. Orban's defeat in April 2026 removes the entity's best
door in the EU, and no source on the new Hungarian government's line toward
Banja Luka was found. The entity's two stable patrons are therefore
Belgrade (kin, bounded) and Moscow (kin, expensive); its transactional ones
are Washington, Budapest, Jerusalem, Ankara and Beijing, none of which has a
treaty with it.

grand_strategy.reading:
Slovakia is the case of a small, trade-dependent member state that uses
the rules of the club it belongs to as its main instrument against the
club. Fico has no army to speak of, no oil, and an export economy
wired into German supply chains; what he has is unanimity. The 2023-26
pattern is therefore linkage: a veto (the 18th and 20th sanctions
packages, Ukraine's loan, the accession clusters) is held until a
concrete good is released - gas guarantees, Druzhba oil, a hearing. That
is Luttwak's paradoxical logic in a small space: the weaker the state,
the more it relies on the one resource, procedure, that its partners
cannot take away without breaking their own rules. But the lever
consumes itself. Hungary under Orban was the other half of the veto
axis; after Magyar's win in April 2026 Bratislava is alone, the
Parliament has asked for conditionality, and the Visegrad revival is
being run by Tusk, Babis and Magyar, not by Fico. Two signals that are
not rows: Fico took the Moscow trip again in May 2026 after having
been shot in 2024 and after a year of mass protest, which shows that
the trips are a message to a domestic electorate and not a
diplomatic programme (OSW and others make this reading of the
American hardware too); and on 18 Sep 2026 he said he would not
be 'part of any military conflict because of Article 5' - a statement
that, if believed, hollows out the alliance whose F-16s he is flying.
The coalition crisis of September 2026 may end the story before the
2027 election: the structural question is whether his successor,
whoever it is, will inherit a state that has learned to veto or one
that has learned to be vetoed.

grand_strategy.reading:
Slovenia is a small, rich, open economy whose strategy is to stay inside every
club (EU, euro, Schengen, NATO) and to spend as little as possible on anything
that is not membership. Its distinctive feature in 2022-26 is that the content
of foreign policy swings with the government while the anchors do not move:
Golob's Slovenia used the Security Council seat to be the EU's most outspoken
critic of Israel; Janša's Slovenia, since June 2026, pays its dues to NATO,
courts Trump and reopens to Israel. One signal that is not a row: Israel's
announced embassy in Ljubljana, the visible reward for the reversal.
What this card could not source and leaves open: Ukraine aid, Western Balkans
advocacy, China, Italy, Trieste and Koper, tariffs and the Hungarian media loan.

grand_strategy.reading: Sweden after 2022 runs the strategy of a small, rich, technologically capable state that has given up the protection of neutrality for the protection of numbers, and is spending to make the swap pay. The organising idea is the Baltic as a NATO lake: Finland, Poland and Denmark are treated as one theatre, the Gripen, the A26 and the CV90 are the instruments of alignment as much as of defence, and the United States is kept inside the system by treaty (the DCA) while Europe is built up for the day it steps back. The Luttwakian pattern is that every step that raises Sweden's value to the alliance also raises its exposure and its bills (the front-line host, the donated Gripens, the loans behind 3.5%), and that the bargains that bought the membership (Turkey, Hungary) taught others that a veto has a price. Two signals are not rows. First, the 13 September 2026 vote ended the Tidö era without producing a successor: the next government will probably keep NATO, Ukraine and the 3.5% target (all large Riksdag majorities) but will change the Israel line and perhaps the EU budget posture, so the card's stability is higher on security than on foreign economic policy. Second, the brief's 'Ukraine 100-year partnership' is not in the record: Sweden's agreement with Ukraine is a ten-year security agreement of May 2024; a 100-year format belongs to the United Kingdom. The Kurdish question behind the accession has faded from the news but not from the memorandum Ankara still holds.

grand_strategy.reading:
Syria under Ahmed al-Sharaa runs the grand strategy of a victorious insurgency
that has to become a state before its patrons lose patience. The rank order of the
objectives is the order of the dangers: first the monopoly of force (the SDF
deal, Suwayda, the coast), then legitimacy (delistings, sanctions relief, Caesar
repeal), then money. The method is multi-alignment at the leader level, with no
patron allowed to own the state: Turkey for the army, the Gulf for the cash,
Washington for the permission to trade, Russia kept only as a training partner,
Iran expelled. The Luttwak pattern is that each move that builds the state
also invites an outsider into it: the Turkish umbrella draws the Israeli strike,
the conquest of the east takes away the American cover, the pressure on
minorities supplies the conditions that Western money carries. Signals that are
not rows: the Syrian army's deployment to the Lebanese border in March 2026,
al-Sharaa's refusal to attend the 2025 Baghdad summit, and Egypt's refusal of a
Syrian ambassador. Open question for the next review: whether the 25 Aug SDF
dissolution survives its first test in Hasakah and Kobani, and whether an
Israeli security agreement is signed or the south settles into a frozen
occupation. Not read in this pass: Crisis Group and Carnegie analyses of 2026
(the search budget ran out), so grades on Israel, Russia and China rest on press
and official statements.

grand_strategy.reading:
Thailand is the textbook of a state that survives by bending: treaty ally of the
United States, economic partner and now arms customer of China, summit
partner of Putin and Modi, comprehensive strategic partner of Vietnam, and it
has not paid the price of joining any camp. What 2025 added is the rest of
Luttwak's lesson: the same state that yields to every great power fought its
small neighbour, and in that war the bending came back. Bangkok held the ground
(Crisis Group: it holds the high ground and land on both sides of the line)
but the end of the war was set in Washington and Putrajaya, by a tariff threat
to both belligerents, and the accord that Trump named for Kuala Lumpur was
suspended by Thailand within a fortnight of signing. The domestic cycle runs on
the same logic. The courts that removed Paetongtarn over a telephone call to
Hun Sen made the border a test of loyalty, Anutin took office on it, called his
election in the middle of the fighting and won 192 seats, and has to govern
with Thaksin's party; the monarchy and Section 112 stay outside every bargain,
the 2026 amnesty included. Adversary or rival: Thailand's grade of Cambodia is
rival, because neither government seeks the other's end (the 27 Dec 2025
statement commits both to demarcation through the Joint Boundary Commission and
ICG's recommendations are about a thaw), though the fighting was the deadliest
between the two in decades. Three signals are not rows: Anutin was the first
ASEAN leader to congratulate Min Aung Hlaing as president (April 2026) and
hosted him in August, a thaw that reverses the 2025 power cut; the United
States put a 12.5% tariff on Thai goods in July 2026 while the reciprocal
agreement is described as 'at the last paragraph'; and the Cambodian frontier
stays shut to trade while both sides insist that the ceasefire holds. Relational
manoeuvre against Thailand therefore does not pass through its alliances but
through its seams: a treaty ally that buys Chinese submarines and Swedish jets,
a neighbour of Cambodia that needs a Malaysian mediator and an American
patron to end its own war, and a junta it needs more than it respects.

grand_strategy.reading:
Türkiye runs the grand strategy of a middle power that has decided to be a hinge
rather than a bloc member: it keeps the second-largest army in NATO and hosts its
2026 summit, buys Russian gas and an S-400, signs a mutual-defence pact with
Riyadh and Islamabad, and offers itself as the venue and mediator that every
side needs. The currency is indispensability, and it works because nobody can
afford to push Ankara out. Luttwak's pattern appears at each seam: the S-400 that
proved autonomy cost the F-35; the victory in Syria draws Israeli bombs on its
airbase; the Blue Homeland decrees imperil the customs union; the boycott of
Israel closes the Gaza seat. Underneath sits regime security. The two things the
leadership most needs in 2026 - the end of the PKK war (Law 7595, the SDF's
dissolution) and a path to keep power (the İmamoğlu trial) - are domestic
before they are foreign, and they set the tone of the external line: a
'Terror-Free Türkiye' that justifies Syrian and Iraqi policy, and a Western
reconciliation (Trump's promise of sanctions relief and the F-35) pursued
without conditions on rule of law. Signals that are not rows: Ankara has not
joined Western sanctions on Russia and cut Russian crude only after Trump's
appeal of Sept 2025; Washington's envoy to Syria is also its ambassador in
Ankara, which makes Turkey the channel for US policy in Damascus. The open
questions for the next quarter are whether Trump's promise becomes a legal
instrument, whether the Blue Homeland law passes in October, and whether the
Israel-Turkey deconfliction mechanism in Syria is built before the next strike.

grand_strategy.reading: Tuvalu's strategy is survival through recognition and treaty, not power: it keeps Taipei against Beijing's pull, binds itself to Canberra through the Falepili Union, and turns the climate case into a claim to statehood in perpetuity. Its budget rests on tuna access, which shrinks as the fish move, on a .tv lease, and on donors it cannot replace, so its freedom of action is largely borrowed. recognition.note: The Republic of China (Taiwan) is recognised by 12 states (the recognition dataset holds 11; the Holy See is written by hand in the Vatican's own file): Paraguay, Guatemala, Belize, Haiti, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, the Marshall Islands, Palau, Tuvalu, Eswatini and the Holy See. It holds no UN seat; Beijing treats it as a province and the great majority of states, including the United States, Japan and the EU members, keep unofficial ties under their own One China formulas.

grand_strategy.reading:
Taiwan is Luttwak's textbook case of a state whose survival rests on two
things it does not control: being indispensable and a guarantor's ambiguity.
The first is real (the leading edge of chips and AI servers) but is traded
away piece by piece to secure the second, and the second is now openly priced:
the Trump administration holds a USD 14bn arms package as a negotiating chip,
says it does not want anyone to 'go independent', and sat down with Xi twice
in 2026 without a word on Taiwan in the White House fact sheet. Beijing, for
its part, has moved from the exercise to the rehearsal of a blockade (Joint
Sword 2024, Strait Thunder 2025A, Justice Mission 2025), and from the
president to the institutions: legal punishment of 'diehards', a channel to
the KMT, and cable and coast-guard pressure in the grey zone. The grade toward
China is therefore rival and not adversary only because Taipei's declared aim
is to be left as it is, not to end the Chinese state, while Beijing's aim is
the end of Taiwan's separateness: the pair is asymmetric on purpose. The home
front is the third hinge: a president whose party lost the legislature, saw
the recalls fail and the budget cut, and whose own parliament now steers part
of the defence plan. Signals that are not rows: no PLA mega-exercise has
followed the Washington summit, air activity is half of 2025 while ships
stay, and Honduras has not decided. The question for 2027 is whether chips
remain a shield or become only a price.

grand_strategy.reading:
Ukraine runs a grand strategy of the weaker party that must make itself
indispensable to stronger ones: it cannot win the war outright, cannot
afford to lose it, and has to keep three patrons (the EU, the UK-led
coalition, the United States) paying while it negotiates with an adversary
whose price is its statehood. At the tactical level it is holding (the
front is slow in 2026, drones and strikes compensate for men), at the
theatre level it is trading minerals, drones and the promise of a rebuilt
country for money and guarantees, and at the grand-strategic level it is
betting that the road to the EU gives it an anchor that no ceasefire can
cancel. Luttwak's reversal is everywhere: the same logic that keeps the
patrons engaged (usefulness, visible strength, deep strikes, a national
story told in battle) irritates the neighbours whose vetoes decide the
anchor, from Fico's pipeline to Warsaw's history. 2026 is also the year the
centre of the question moved from the front to the table: talks opened
in Abu Dhabi in January, were frozen by the Iran war in March, and resumed
with the Miami round of 9-10 October, while the Kremlin still demands the
Donbas. Two signals that are not rows: the new Hungarian government's
shift from veto to conditions (Magyar, since May) and the Ankara
summit's quiet re-labelling of Ukraine as a contributor to Euro-Atlantic
security. Open question for the next review: whether the 15 Oct European
Council and the Miami outcome change the guarantee from a text to a force.

grand_strategy.reading: The United States in October 2026 runs the most explicit grand strategy it has published since the Cold War, and the one most at odds with its own means. The ends are written down: a hemisphere held under a Trump Corollary, trade rebalanced by tariff, China kept a rival 'within bounds', Europe's defence handed to Europeans, the Middle East managed without forever wars, migration ended. At the technical level the instruments work - the border is quieter than in fifty years, allies have pledged trillions and 5% of GDP, Maduro sits in a Brooklyn cell, Khamenei is dead. At the level of grand strategy the picture inverts, as Luttwak says it must when a strategy succeeds: coercion used on everyone reached its culminating point in a year (Davos, Spain, the Supreme Court), the allies who paid became hedgers, the war of choice against Iran consumed the year that was reserved for the hemisphere and China, and the hemisphere itself produced a Venezuela that Washington now administers. Three signals that are not rows: the NDS never names Taiwan; the USMCA was left unrenewed on 1 July without any plan for what follows; and the same government that sanctioned Rosneft is buying Russian diesel. Washington's stances read accordingly: one adversary (Iran), two rivals it talks to more than to its allies (China, Russia), and a ring of treaty allies graded reluctant not because they resist the alliance but because Washington does - the first great power in the atlas whose friction with its allies is mostly its own.

grand_strategy.reading:
Uzbekistan is the one state in the region whose strategy is a strategy of
position: doubly landlocked, the most populous in Central Asia and the youngest
of the big populations (a median age near 27), it has turned its geography
from a prison into a toll. Luttwak's logic runs the other way from the
great powers' - the weak do not win by force but by being the crossing that
several strong actors each need and none can take. Since 2016 Mirziyoyev
has traded the Karimov-era isolation for a portfolio of partners (Carnegie's
word for it): rail to China, rail to Pakistan through Afghanistan, Rosatom and
Gazprom for power, Gulf money for solar, Washington and Brussels for minerals
and legitimacy, Seoul and Tokyo for factories, Delhi for the Indian Ocean route
and a Treaty on Allied Relations with each Turkic neighbour that is not an
alliance in the military sense. The 2023 constitution is the domestic hinge:
the opening abroad is the means by which a reset presidency keeps its
stability. The paradoxes all take the same shape - each exit from one
dependence is an entry into another: Russian power for Russian gas, Chinese rail
for Chinese goods, the Taliban corridor for the Taliban's canal, remittances for
Russia's lever. The gold reserve is the one buffer that belongs to Tashkent
alone, and the central bank's decision to keep it at home tells how it
reads the risk. Watch two signals that are not rows: the 17% of the Chinese
railway built by August 2026 (the first real test of whether the toll works) and
the 29-30 Oct Ankara summit of the Turkic states after Mirziyoyev's trip to
Ashgabat for the CIS summit (7-9 Oct, outcomes unconfirmed).

grand_strategy.reading: The Holy See has no army and no military allies, so its grand strategy is diplomatic and moral: keep 184 states talking to it, keep the Church alive where it is restricted, and make the pope's voice count in wars it cannot stop. Under Leo XIV, elected on 8 May 2025 as the first American-born pope, the line continues Francis but is sharper on migration and Gaza, and it accepts cooler relations with Washington as the price. The weak points are money (a structural deficit covered by Peter's Pence) and China, where the 2018 deal is the main file and the clearest case of a channel kept open at the cost of its text. Recognition is the currency it trades: Taiwan (one of the few states with relations with the Republic of China), Palestine since 2015, and the Lebanon and Turkey trip of late 2025 as a way to speak to Middle East Christians. Non-events to watch: no US visit was planned for 2026, and the Ukraine talks offer in Vatican City has not been accepted by Moscow.

grand_strategy.reading: Vietnam is the state that fought the two great powers of the twentieth century and now sells its neutrality to both of them, plus everyone in between. Luttwak's logic of strategy predicts a small state next to a giant to either bandwagon or build a coalition; Hanoi does something third: it builds a web of eleven comprehensive strategic partnerships, refuses every alliance, and spends its leverage on becoming indispensable rather than protected. Indispensability is real - it is the electronics platform of Samsung and other foreign groups, the Spratly claimant with the most reclaimed land after China, the rice and seafood exporter, the 100-million-strong market - but it is paid for in dependence on both markets: China supplies 40% of its imports, the US takes the largest share of its exports. The 2026 novelty is domestic. To Lam's double crown (Party chief since August 2024 and State President since 7 April 2026, the 14th Congress behind him, the districts abolished) lets Hanoi decide faster and hedge more loudly - Washington in February, Beijing in April, ASEAN capitals in May and June, Moscow and Paris in September - and with the same speed it removes the collective brake that made the balance credible. Two signals are not rows: the Supreme Court's February 2026 ruling that cancelled the legal basis of the 20% tariff left Vietnam holding a deal whose price Washington can rebuild by other means, and the August 2026 Chinese completion of Antelope Reef shows that Hanoi's own island-building did not deter Beijing. Hanoi's bet is that Beijing will keep tolerating a smaller neighbour that is good for Chinese manufacturing; its fear is that the Americans will treat it as a transshipment point and the Russians as a customer. Open question for 2027: whether the partners other than China will stay content with signed documents, or start to demand that Vietnam choose a side.

grand_strategy.reading: Samoa is a small state whose security sits in a 1962 treaty with New Zealand, whose money comes from remittances and from Australian and Chinese lending, and whose labour schemes send thousands of its people to work in New Zealand and Australia. The 2025 crisis changed who governs without changing that frame: Fiame Naomi Mataafa's government lost its budget vote on 27 May 2025, a snap election on 29 August gave FAST 30 seats (31 with a later defector) out of 51, and the FAST faction led by Laauli Leuatea Schmidt, which had split from Mataafa earlier in 2025, became the government on 16 September. At the UN the atlas records yes votes on all six Ukraine landmark resolutions from 2022 to 2026 and an abstention on the September 2024 resolution ending Israel's presence in the occupied Palestinian territory. The stage is the Commonwealth summit that Samoa hosted in Apia in October 2024, and no sourced foreign-policy line from the Schmidt government has been found beyond its March 2026 dispute with New Zealand over a matai title.

grand_strategy.reading:
Kosovo runs the strategy of a state that exists on the ground and not yet in
law: every move is a bid to turn effective control into recognised status, and
the only currencies it has are loyalty and usefulness to the West. That
produces the central Luttwakian pattern: the actions that prove statehood
(mayors in the north, the army, rail stations, the war-memory law) are the
ones that cost it the patrons who could confer it, while the actions that would
please the patrons (the Community of Serb-majority Municipalities, Serbian
return to the judiciary) are those it fears would hollow out statehood from
within. Since 2025 the pressure has eased on one flank (EU measures lifted in
March 2026, institutions completed in September-October) and tightened on
another (KFOR shrinking, a cooler Washington, the Specialist Chambers
verdicts). Two signals that are not rows: the US launched a strategic dialogue with
Belgrade on 17 July 2026 although Kosovo had joined the Board of Peace and
pledged troops to Gaza, and the 6 Oct law on the Hague court was passed under
street pressure, not diplomatic calculation. With
the 25 Oct Serbian election ahead, Pristina's real question is whether the
stalled Ohrid road can be re-opened by a new government in Belgrade.

grand_strategy.reading:
The internationally recognised government of Yemen is a state held up from outside: legal
seat at the UN, salaries and grants from Riyadh, air power largely Saudi, and most of its people
beyond its writ. Its grand strategy is therefore less a plan than a position in a Saudi
plan, and Luttwak's levels diverge sharply. At the theatre level the goal is the
Houthis' defeat (the PLC's own word is the 'decisive phase', 4 Oct 2026); at the
grand-strategic level the goal is to remain the party Riyadh must keep, against a
Houthi movement that Riyadh has negotiated with since 2022 and against an Emirati
network it destroyed in January 2026. The 2026 sequence is the paradox of the card:
the elimination of the STC bought Saudi control of the south and left the camp
without its best money and units, then the coast fell within a week; the Iran war
turned the Bab al-Mandab into a bargaining chip, so that the contest over Yemen's
coast is settled in Tehran, Riyadh, Washington and Muscat as much as in Taiz and
Mokha. What decides the next year is Saudi stamina and Saudi pain: the government
needs the offensive to continue and cannot control the price Riyadh pays. Signals
that are not rows: the Houthis' own account of their aims (Sanaa-based media only,
not researched); the Southern movement after the STC's formal dissolution, which
appears in the sources only as protest and bombings; the UAE's silence on Yemen
since January except for condemning the strikes on Saudi airports.

grand_strategy.reading:
South Africa under Ramaphosa's government of national unity has moved from a balance between the West and the Global South to a deliberate Global South stance, with the ICJ case, BRICS and the 2025 G20 presidency as its instruments of standing. The United States is its main rival in 2025-26, but the rivalry runs on tariffs, aid and the Afrikaner refugee question rather than on existence, and the AGOA lapse shows how cheaply Washington can apply pressure. China is the commercial anchor, and the trade deal in preparation is the test of whether Pretoria can turn minerals into value. The constraints are at home (the grid, the rand, a stalled economy) and in the neighbourhood (Nigeria's leadership claim, a withdrawn DRC force), so the stance is louder than the capacity behind it.

Added in the protagonist pass (16 October 2026). The 2025-26 pattern is a state that hosts the superpower's rivals and still wants the superpower's market: the G20 gavel was used against Washington, a China-led naval exercise with Russia and Iran was held in South African waters, and the answer to each accusation is a process (an inquiry, a board, a declaration) rather than a change of line. Europe, the UK and Germany took a different view from the US over the same record, so the break is bilateral, not Western. The clock is AGOA on 31 December 2026 and the local elections of the coming weeks, which test whether the unity government can still carry one voice. In the neighbourhood the state is stronger than its economy suggests: it chairs SADC, supplies the market and the currency, and has the bi-national commissions to prove it.

Lusaka keeps two export routes open at once: the US-backed Lobito corridor to the Atlantic and the China-backed TAZARA revival to Dar es Salaam. The 2026 election was fought on the cost of living, which only copper output and reliable power can pay for.

means.text: Copper and the mines. Copper is the economy and the export earner; Lusaka's lever is the mines' output and the price, and the state utility ZESCO decides how much of it runs. Power is the bottleneck: the state utility rationed electricity to mining firms as Lake Kariba fell, and the Chambishi smelter (CNMC) cut a fifth of its output in March 2024 for lack of power. The reported 2025 power deficit was about 707 MW (a press figure, not checked against the utility).

The US-backed Lobito corridor has a USD 553m DFC loan to the LAR consortium; the China-backed TAZARA concession of about USD 1.4bn (30 years) was signed in Beijing on 29 September 2025. Lusaka sits at the centre of both and keeps its seats in the African Union, SADC and the Commonwealth, the forums where it is a frontline-state voice rather than a client.

constraints.text: The drought is a physical limit. Lake Kariba's fall cuts hydro output, the state utility has rationed power to the mines, and the mines are first in line when the grid is short. Growth and copper output are capped by megawatts, not by the state's diplomacy.

paradoxes.text: The copper plan needs power, yet both corridors Lusaka courts depend on the same grid that the drought has cut: the Chambishi smelter lost a fifth of its output to power shortages in 2024 while Zambia bid for a US line and a Chinese line at once. The more rails Lusaka secures, the more it needs megawatts to fill them.

grand_strategy.reading: Zambia's grand strategy is to turn world demand for copper into revenue and room to manoeuvre: keep the American Atlantic route and the Chinese route to Dar es Salaam open at once, so that no single rail line, lender or buyer holds the mines. The binding limits are physical and financial rather than diplomatic, since the drought-hit hydro grid and the IMF cycle decide how much copper moves and how much reform Hichilema, re-elected on 18 August 2026 with about 61% in a contested count, can afford. The paradox is that the two corridors depend on the same power the drought has cut, so the strategy is only as strong as the next dry season.

constraints.text: US sanctions and ZIDERA. In March 2024 the US designated eight individuals, Mnangagwa among them, and three businesses under the Global Magnitsky Act. constraints.text: A single buyer for the mineral chain. Most of Zimbabwe's lithium output goes to China and Chinese firms own the largest mines, so Beijing's processors set the terms of the value chain the export ban is meant to build. The 2022 USD 180m purchase of Bikita Minerals by Sinomine is the best-known case.

paradoxes.text: The export ban meant to keep value at home favours the Chinese-financed plants that can afford processing. A Bikita community leader sees no tangible jobs from value addition, and smaller miners warn that processing plants, unreliable power and scarce finance keep them out, so the policy meant to widen the base may concentrate it.

grand_strategy.reading: Zimbabwe's grand strategy is the survival of the ZANU-PF system under Mnangagwa: the 2026 amendment extends his rule to 2030 by moving the choice of president from voters to parliament. Its money comes from minerals, above all lithium, that flow mostly to China, which funds and buys the extraction, while the Western sanctions that remain (the 2024 Global Magnitsky listings and ZIDERA) keep the other door narrow. The export ban is the state's attempt to turn that dependence into domestic value, and the paradox is that the Chinese-financed plants are the ones best placed to benefit from it.

AFG.note: Pakistan was the Taliban's patron and sanctuary; since 9 Oct 2025 (first Pakistani strike on Kabul) it is the Emirate's main military enemy: border war in October 2025, Doha/Istanbul ceasefire talks that failed, 'open war' declared by Khawaja Asif on 26-27 Feb 2026 with strikes on Kabul and Kandahar, a truce from 18 Mar, talks in Urumqi in April, new strikes on 24 Sep 2026; borders mostly closed since 12 Oct 2025; over 2.4 million Afghans returned from Pakistan since 2023. Zelin (WINEP, Aug 2026) says Pakistan went 'from patron to adversary' - a source that uses the stronger word. Adversary test: the grade stays rival because neither side's declared aim is the other's disappearance. Islamabad says borders reopen on 'decisive and verifiable action' against the TTP and keeps attending China-, Qatar-, Turkey- and Saudi-mediated talks; Kabul says it is 'open to talks', sends delegations, and treats the TTP as Pakistan's internal affair. Asif's 'obliterate' and 'open war' lines and the Taliban's claim that Pakistan backs anti-Taliban fronts are the argument for adversary and are the reason the trend is cooling and the confidence C; if Pakistan states a regime-change aim or Kabul seeks Pakistani territory, regrade. Bond - grievance: the TTP sanctuary, deportations, the Durand Line, the trade closures. Asymmetric pairing with PAK's own side is expected to differ (Islamabad is likely to grade Kabul adversary).

AND.note: Treaty-based: the 1993 Treaty of Good Neighbourliness, Friendship and Cooperation with Spain and France, and the constitution that makes the French president one of the two co-princes. The co-princely link is older (the 1607 edict, the 1278 pareatge), but the 1993 treaty is the standing legal tie, so since is 1993. France and Andorra have had diplomatic relations since 3 June 1993. Bond - affinity: a shared Romance-language and cultural space and a long habit of co-sovereignty, not kinship. The French co-prince holds the office by virtue of being president of France; Andorran voters do not choose either co-prince.

CHN.note: Rival, the atlas's reference case for the grade (ONTOLOGY: 'the US toward China'), read here from Beijing: competition over technology, trade, Taiwan and the order, no will to destroy the other. Beijing's own words are 'healthy competition kept within bounds' and no 'Thucydides trap' (Xi, Washington, 24 Sep 2026); its structure is a chip embargo it cannot answer in kind, an 'affiliates rule' and a 47% tariff wall answered with rare-earth licences and the market. Warming because three summits in eleven months (Busan 30 Oct 2025, Beijing 14-16 May 2026, Washington 23-25 Sep 2026) each extended the truce, launched a Board of Trade and an AI dialogue, cut tariffs on about USD 30bn of goods and put military-to-military channels back; Brookings reads Xi as preferring 'anemic stability to no stability at all'. Not partner: the truce is a pause on each side's weapons (soybeans excluded, magnets 20% below trend, the arms package to Taiwan 'in abeyance' but not withdrawn), not an alignment. Bond - grievance: the Taiwan Relations Act and arms sales since 1979, the 1999 Belgrade embassy bombing and the 'containment' narrative are the standing wound in Beijing's reading, whatever the mood of the summit.

CZE.note: Russia is named the main security threat by BIS (annual report for 2025, published Aug 2026) and Prague has expelled its diplomats (18 in April 2021 over Vrbetice, Russia answered with 20 and an 'unfriendly' listing), sanctioned its influence network (Voice of Europe, 2024) and cut oil and gas imports to zero. But the grade is rival, not adversary: no Czech government has declared Russia's defeat or regime change as the aim, and the Babiš cabinet slowed the anti-Russia machinery (sanctions unit dissolved, diplomat restrictions delayed until Moscow tightened its own on 3 Sep 2026). Trend stable: hawkish state organs, softer cabinet. Bond - grievance: 1968 and Vrbetice.

CZE.note: Under Fiala Czechia was close to an ally (the ammunition initiative, the 2025 Unity Hub in Prague). Under Babiš it is a partner that has stopped paying: coordinator of the shell channel with no state money (Jan 2026), opt-out from the guarantees for the EUR 90bn EU loan (19 Dec 2025), L-159 transfer shelved, a speaker (Okamura) calling Kyiv's leadership a 'junta' (Ukraine summoned the Czech chargé on 5 Jan 2026, then both agreed to 'turn the page'), and a bill tightening Ukrainian refugees' benefits for 1 Jan 2027. Still not a rival: the channel runs, Pavel and the army back Kyiv, and the cabinet says Ukraine needs help if others pay. Bond - affinity: a large Ukrainian refugee community and the 2025 Unity Hub in Prague.

Friction is real - Berlin's Green Deal and the 2035 engine ban are what the Babiš cabinet attacks, and the cabinet's migration and Ukraine-funding lines differ - but it does not change the structure; Czech security and industry sit on the German side. Bond - affinity: dependence, shared border, centuries of exchange.

Under Fiala the two diverged over Ukraine (Fico opposed aid); under Babiš Prague moved toward Bratislava rather than the reverse, opting out together on the EU loan. Residual friction: Fico's bid to stop the Ukraine loan, Czech ammunition work for Kyiv. Bond - kin: a common state until 1992.

Friction: Warsaw is the loudest Ukraine supporter in the region while the Czech cabinet has stopped paying, and the V4 had been paralysed by that split under Fiala. Stable because both want the V4 back in a form that excludes the Ukraine question. Bond - affinity: the Visegrad tie, shared eastern-flank worries.

CZE.note: Treaty ally (Article 5) since 1999 and the cabinet says it will honour its commitments; the friction is the bill. NATO is also where the cabinet would like Ukraine's ammunition financing to move. The grade stays ally: no source, including the Ankara summit assessments, questions membership. CZE.note: The most pro-Israel government in the EU: the coalition programme speaks of a 'special relationship', Foreign Minister Macinka said in December 2025 that the embassy should move to Jerusalem in 2026 (he said in May that he wants it in his mandate but it is a cabinet decision), Sa'ar met Babiš on 19 Jan 2026 and called him 'courageous and exceptional', and Prague opened a Jerusalem office in 2021. Czechia abstained (not voted no) on the 12 Sep 2025 UNGA endorsement of the New York two-state declaration, objecting that Israel was not involved. Graded partner, not ally: there is no treaty or guarantee and no source calls it an alliance. Bond - affinity: a long record of pro-Israel positions (the lone European no vote on Palestine's UN upgrade in 2012, the unanimous parliamentary resolution of Oct 2023 urging the embassy move).

DEU.note: Germany's 2023 National Security Strategy calls Russia the greatest threat to peace in the Euro-Atlantic area for the foreseeable future, Pistorius puts a possible Russian attack on NATO at 2029 or earlier, and the federal prosecutor has charged sabotage and espionage plots in 2025-26 (three men over rail sabotage, a Kazakh national in Berlin; 165+ suspected incidents in 2026 per SZ). Not 'adversary': the same strategy says Germany and NATO do not seek hostility or confrontation, and Berlin's declared aim is deterrence and Ukraine's survival, not Russia's defeat or the end of its regime (compare Poland's 'adversary' and the Czech and Croatian 'rival'). No source uses the word 'rival': the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C), one step from adversary. Bond - grievance: the war and the Nord Stream dependence Berlin now regrets.

Merz says personal relations with Trump are good. Cooling, but Berlin has no alternative guarantor. Bond - affinity.

DZA.note: Argued from Algiers' side. Algeria cut diplomatic relations on 24 Aug 2021 over Morocco's 'hostile actions' (it blamed the August 2021 wildfires on the MAK, which it labels terrorist, and accused Rabat of backing it), the border has been shut since 1994, the Maghreb-Europe gas contract was left to lapse on 31 Oct 2021, Tebboune said in Mar 2023 that ties had passed 'the point of no return', the airspace was closed to Moroccan aircraft on 22 Sep 2021 and visas were imposed on Moroccans on 26 Sep 2024, and in Nov 2025 Attaf said bilateral dialogue with Morocco 'is not on the agenda' while Washington mediates; S/RES/2797 names Algeria among the parties it asks to negotiate. The Kabylie charge is the nearest Algiers comes to an existential accusation. But the ontology's test for adversary is a declared aim of the other's defeat or disappearance: Algiers declares Sahrawi self-determination, border security and the military balance, not Moroccan partition or regime change; the king has repeatedly offered to talk; Carnegie and Crisis Group speak of a rivalry (Carnegie: extending into the Sahel) and SIPRI of a long-running tension that drives arms imports, not of a war aim. Rival, stable (frozen); the grade would move to adversary only if Algiers stated an aim against Moroccan integrity or Rabat's MAK backing were proved and acted on. Bond - grievance: Western Sahara, the Sand War legacy and mutual accusation.

EST.note: Rival, not adversary: Estonia's aim is deterrence, a Russian defeat in Ukraine and payment of damages, not the end of the Russian state or its regime; it keeps a border regime and diplomatic contact (chargé d'affaires summoned). The friction is the sharpest in the Baltic: MiG-31 intrusion and Article 4 request (19 Sep 2025), the Jaguar/Su-35 episode (May 2025), GPS jamming, the Milrem arson blamed on Russian services (Sep 2026), the Estlink 2 cut. Estonian foreign intelligence calls Russia the main threat but judges it has no intention to attack in the coming year; the Kremlin says it poses no threat to Estonia. No source uses 'rival': the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C), and Moscow's side (RUS card) is expected to grade Estonia more harshly - an asymmetric pair that is deliberate. Bond - grievance: the Soviet occupation and Russian claim to protect Russian speakers.

EST.note: Treaty ally under NATO Article 5 with a rotational US presence of over 600 troops; but the trend is cooling. The Pentagon cancelled the Poland-bound rotation from which part of the US contingent in Estonia was to come (5,000-troop drawdown, May 2026), Estonian public trust in Trump is low, and the future of the US presence after the rotation ending in 2026 is under review, while Pevkur says he trusts the US and does not expect withdrawal. Friction is about the commitment, not the structure, so ally and not reluctant ally. Bond - affinity: US non-recognition of the Soviet annexation and 30 years of security partnership.

ETH.note: Mirror of the Egyptian file, with Addis Ababa's side added. The Nile is the oldest quarrel: the GERD (inaugurated 9 Sep 2025, USD 5bn, after the Egyptian and Sudanese foreign ministers had urged Ethiopia to change course) is built, three more Blue Nile dams were announced in March 2026, and on 1 Oct 2026 Ethiopia expelled an Egyptian diplomat on the day it accused Egypt, Eritrea and Sudan of backing the seven-group opposition alliance (Egypt denies it and expelled an Ethiopian counsellor). Addis Ababa's reading is that Egypt is encircling it - the Somalia pact of Aug 2024, AUSSOM troops, Eritrea, Sudan, the El Alamein summit of 4 Oct - and its foreign ministry answers that talks on the Nile and the Red Sea must reflect geography. Rival, not adversary: Addis Ababa contests Egypt's veto over the Nile, not Egypt's existence or regime, and says it stays committed to dialogue; Cairo likewise asks for 'dialogue, not confrontation'. Trump offered to restart GERD mediation at Davos (Jan 2026). Bond grievance: the water.

ETH.note: Argued grade, and mutual: the Eritrean card (review regrade of 2026-10-16) reads Ethiopia as adversary too, at confidence C. Not a partner to be repaired: on 1 Oct 2026 Ethiopia shut its embassy in Asmara and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats citing 'direct and indirect acts of hostility and belligerence', Eritrea severed relations, and on 8-9 Oct Addis Ababa told the UN Security Council that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray ('a blatant act of aggression' engaging its Article 51 right of self-defence), while it says Asmara finances, arms and directs the armed groups whose declared aim is the overthrow of the government. Eritrea answers that Ethiopia has 'declared war' to seize Assab. Why adversary and not rival: on Addis Ababa's own account the other side is a sponsor of a coalition seeking to remove the regime and an invader, the diplomatic channel is closed, and an analyst (Gardner, The Economist) places the moment as the most dangerous since the 1998-2000 war and reads Ethiopia's goal as including the removal of Eritrea's government from the picture. Why only B: the Eritrean incursion and the sponsorship are Addis Ababa's allegations, unverified (Rompel), Abiy publicly says no bullet will be fired at Eritrea and no source shows a declared aim to end the Eritrean state; the grade falls to rival if the embassies reopen or the UN channel produces a withdrawal. Bond grievance: 1998-2000, Eritrea's exclusion from Pretoria and its brief 2020-22 alliance, which Gardner calls an exception.

ETH.note: Transactional cooperation after a rupture: the MoU with Somaliland (1 Jan 2024) broke relations, the Turkish-mediated Ankara Declaration (11 Dec 2024) restored them with Ethiopia pledging respect for Somalia's sovereignty and Somalia a sea-access route under its own authority, and Ethiopian troops stayed in AUSSOM (2,500 allocated). Hassan Sheikh Mohamud attended the GERD launch (Sept 2025), sat in the Jigjiga trilateral (31 Jan 2026) and met Abiy in Addis Ababa the day before his Djibouti talks of 30 Sep (about 29 Sep), but then signed at El Alamein (4 Oct) a text rejecting any support for Somaliland and writing the 'coastal states only' Red Sea principle - hence cooling. The counter-signal came the next day: he congratulated Abiy on his oath and said Somalia does not object to Ethiopian access to the Red Sea through Somali territory if it is negotiated formally. Addis Ababa's own red line is Gedo: it warned in Oct 2025 that a rival Jubaland administration there would be a direct threat. Partner, not reluctant partner: Addis Ababa neither resists nor seeks alignment, it needs Mogadishu out of the Egyptian camp. The Somali card reads Ethiopia as a reluctant partner with a grievance bond, stable (mirrored: same sources), and Egypt's own file grades Somalia a partner and a client: Mogadishu sits at both tables. Bond none.

ETH.note: Sudan's army government recalled its ambassador from Addis Ababa on 5 May 2026, accused Ethiopia and the UAE of drone attacks launched from Bahir Dar (three drones from 1 March, one downed near El Obeid on 17 March, one on Khartoum airport in May) and its foreign minister said Sudan was 'ready to enter into an open confrontation'; Addis Ababa called the accusations 'baseless' and, for the first time, accused the Sudanese army of arming 'mercenaries' against the central government in Tigray. Behind the drones lies the RSF war: Reuters reported on 10 Feb 2026 a secret camp in Ethiopia (Menge district, Benishangul-Gumuz) training thousands of RSF fighters with Emirati money, and a Yale Humanitarian Research Lab report of April 2026 read satellite images of the Asosa base as consistent with military assistance to the RSF; Ethiopia denies hosting RSF camps or allowing attacks from its soil, and the UAE role is unverified. Khartoum's card reads Ethiopia as a rival with a grievance bond (al-Fashaga, the GERD) and cooling, and names Ethiopian-backed militia incursions in al-Fashaga (Jul 2025). Sudan stands at El Alamein (4 Oct), on the Egyptian side, and the old al-Fashaga farmland dispute remains unresolved, with the Sudanese army reinforcing the Gedaref frontier in May. Rival, not adversary: Ethiopia publicly calls for dialogue among Sudan's warring parties, and neither side declares an aim of ending the other - each accuses the other of arming its enemies, a proxy quarrel short of mortal enmity. Bond grievance (changed from none at the 2026-10-16 review, mirroring the Sudanese card): the unresolved al-Fashaga border district and the Nile.

ETH.note: Djibouti handled 96.7% of Ethiopia's external freight in FY2025/26 and the two states keep the corridor: Abiy at Doraleh port in January 2026, the Jigjiga trilateral with Guelleh and Hassan Sheikh on 31 Jan, a Doraleh cooperation agreement in Feb 2026. The strain is the sea-access push: Djibouti offered a 60% stake in the Tadjoura port and, by its account, Addis Ababa declined, wanting a corridor on top of equity (Capital Ethiopia, Apr 2026); Djibouti's own card calls the push an existential risk for it, and fighting in the north in late September 2026 was reported near the routes that link Ethiopia with Djibouti. A dependence in both directions that Ethiopia wants to dilute (Berbera, Lamu, Assab) without breaking. Partner, not ally; Egypt's file also treats Djibouti as a partner, so Cairo's tie is a lever on Ethiopia's only door. Bond none.

Federal forces and the Tigray Peace Force retook Mekelle on 3-4 Oct after the TPLF withdrew; Debretsion says the fight continues as 'mobile' war. Adversary: the other side's declared aim is the end of the government, and the federal side has answered by marching on Mekelle and backing the anti-TPLF Tigray Peace Force; the Pretoria agreement that formally binds both is not observed. Bond grievance: the 2020-22 war and its 500,000 civilian dead (Ghent estimate).

ETH.note: Argued grade, low confidence. Adversary and not rival because the other side's declared aim is the end of the government and the federal answer is war, including the Afar and Amhara fronts. Why only C: no source read gives a formal terrorist designation of Fano (the OLA and the TPLF were designated in May 2021); Fano is a set of commands rather than one body, and commanders near Western Tigray may not accept an alliance with Tigray (Al Jazeera). Bond grievance: the 2023 disarmament order, the Western Tigray question and the killings of Oromo civilians in Wollega that Fano is accused of.

FIN.note: Why rival and not adversary: Finland's own line is that Russia is not an enemy but its actions and breaches of international law are opposed (Valtonen, April 2025), and the declared strategy is to support Ukraine, weaken Russia through sanctions and strengthen defence - deterrence and containment, not an aim of Russia's defeat or regime. Yet the Government Defence Report (Dec 2024) calls Russia a long-term threat that will outlast the war, Supo names it the main threat, the eastern border has been shut since December 2023, Russia closed five rail crossings on 1 Jul 2026, and Peskov says Finland and Sweden 'reduced relations to zero'. Stubb (31 Mar 2025) says Finns must prepare mentally for an eventual thaw, so the door is not closed. Bond - grievance: Winter War memory and the 1,340 km border, now sharpened by hybrid pressure (instrumentalised migration, GNSS jamming, cable incidents). Our reading of the grade is C-level on the word itself; the structure is documented by tier 1 sources.

FJI.note: Partner, not reluctant partner: the cooperation is transactional (fisheries, police training) and Fiji resists Chinese officers inside its force, not alignment itself. Rabuka cited Australia and NZ as partners with comparable systems (SCMP). A 2025 Chinese-side release says more than 100 Chinese vessels use Fiji as a base; it is promotional and tier 4. GBR.note: NATO ally, Trident and intelligence partner, signer of the May 2025 Economic Prosperity Deal and the Sept 2025 Tech Prosperity Deal (state visit at Windsor, about GBP 150bn of pledges) - the structure is alliance. But the friction is now visible and two-sided: London refused the US the use of its bases for the first strikes on Iran (28 Feb 2026; Diego Garcia then opened for 'specific and limited defensive purposes') and Trump said the relationship was 'obviously not what it was'; the UK paused Caribbean intelligence sharing in Nov 2025 over the boat strikes; Washington has withheld consent on Chagos; a leaked Pentagon email in April 2026 suggested a review of the Falklands position (the State Department then said 'neutrality'); the IEEPA tariffs fell in Feb 2026 and Section 301 action naming the UK followed on 23 Jul. Diplomats quoted in the press call the relationship 'very damaged'; Burnham met Trump at the UN on 22 Sep 2026 and both described it warmly, while Burnham says he will call Trump out when Britain's interest requires. Reluctant ally because the dependency (Trident, F-35A, GPS and intelligence) keeps the UK aligned against its present preference. Bond - affinity: language, history, intelligence and nuclear kinship; no grievance.

HTI.note: Viv Ansanm, formed in September 2023 by G9 and G-Pèp, was created to attack the Haitian government (police stations, government buildings, infrastructure) and to fight the international force (Wikipedia, tier 4). Adversary is our reading, not a source's word, and it is the rare grade by design: the sources show hostile attacks on the state, not a stated aim of replacing it, so if a stricter reading is taken this becomes rival. Bond none: no kinship or affinity is named. Trend stable: the 2026 coverage shows continued killings, with no sign of a turn.

HTI.note: Mirror of the KEN card's stance toward HTI (same sources, read from Haiti's side). Kenya led the Multinational Security Support mission from June 2024 and the Security Council turned it into the Gang Suppression Force on 30 September 2025; the Haitian state receives Kenyan police, and Kenya's second contingent came home in March 2026 with Chad replacing it. Partner and not ally: a service to the Haitian state, not an alliance. Cooling because the mission is winding down, with Haitian protests against the Kenyan exit reported in April 2026. Confidence C: this is our reading of the structure; the departure status after April 2026 is unconfirmed. Bond none.

HTI.note: Washington is the patron of the post-transition arrangement: it backed Prime Minister Fils-Aime staying on after the council's mandate ended on 7 February 2026, threatened serious consequences against any removal and sanctioned five council members (Reuters, via Citizen Digital). Its funding of the force is not confirmed by any source reached here, so it is not stated. It is the major trading partner under HOPE and HELP (Wikipedia). Cooling is our reading from the 2026 terminations: the US has moved to end Temporary Protected Status for Haitians, and the Supreme Court in June 2026 let the termination for Haiti proceed (Wikipedia, tier 4). Partner, not ally: transactional and interest-based. Bond none: no source names a kinship or an open wound between the pair. The since date is the 2026 backing; the trade partnership is older. HUN.note: Member since 2004, so the 'partner' grade of non-members does not apply; the co-member rule gives reluctant_ally while friction remains. Sixteen years of vetoes and Article 7 ended with the 12 Apr 2026 election (Tisza 53%, 138 of 199 seats; 'the Hungarian people have said yes to Europe'). The Commission proposed on 23 Sep 2026 to release EUR 4.2bn of the funds frozen since 2022 and the Council meets on 13 Oct; EUR 3.5bn is still blocked over the child-protection, academic-freedom and asylum files, and Hungary's court case against the EU's Russian gas ban and the migration-pact fight show the friction is not over. Bond affinity: a government that wants to be inside, not a rebel.

HUN.note: NATO ally, so not 'partner'. Washington was Orban's patron: Vance campaigned for him days before the vote, Trump gave him a one-year waiver on Russian oil and gas sanctions and an open-ended one for Paks II in Nov 2025 against US LNG and nuclear-fuel purchases. After the vote Trump called Magyar 'a good man' and the US embassy promised close cooperation, but no White House invitation is reported, a pro-Fidesz outlet describes a missed handshake at the Ankara summit, and the waiver lapses on 21 Nov 2026 with Budapest asking for an extension. The 'cooling' is a reading of lost patronage, not a US act (confidence C). Bond affinity: the Biden-era freeze is over and migration politics still overlaps.

HUN.note: Treaty-based strategic partnership (2021) with a defence agreement (2023, implementing agreement 2025) that Belgrade reads as an alliance and Telex calls 'a far cry from' one; Serbia grades Hungary 'ally'. The structural facts: Serbian TurkStream gas passes to Hungary, MOL is buying Gazprom Neft's 56.15% of NIS, the Chinese-built Budapest-Belgrade railway is delayed, and Vojvodina's Hungarians keep Budapest attached. After 12 Apr 2026 the tone is cordial at government level (Vucic phone call, July ambassador farewell) but Magyar hinted Vucic's 'godfather' relationship with Orban and Fico, and Vucic retorted that Serbia is not Magyar's country. Cooling because the personal patron is gone. Bond affinity: Vojvodina's minority and the shared sovereigntist camp.

IND.note: The ontology's adversary test: does New Delhi seek the end of the Pakistani state or its regime? The record says no. After the Pahalgam attack (22 Apr 2025, 26 killed, claimed by TRF, which India calls a Lashkar-e-Taiba front) India struck nine 'terrorist sites' in Operation Sindoor on 7 May 2025, fought four days of missile, drone and artillery exchanges, and then accepted a ceasefire agreed between the two DGMOs on 10 May; it targets terror infrastructure and the army's sponsorship of it, calls the new line 'if Pakistan fires, we fire', and keeps the Pakistani state as the counterpart it holds responsible. The Indus Waters Treaty is 'in abeyance' since 23 Apr 2025 'until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures cross-border terrorism' (MEA, 3 Jul 2026) - leverage with a stated exit condition, not an end-state. India does claim all of Jammu and Kashmir including Pakistan-held territory, and engagement is now limited to terrorism and PoK. After the Red Fort car bomb in Delhi (10 Nov 2025, 12-15 killed, a Jaish-e-Mohammed link noted by the UN monitoring team in Feb 2026) India did not formally blame Pakistan or retaliate, which shows the threshold is attribution, not each incident. That is a rivalry with a nuclear shadow and an arms race, not a war of existence, so `rival`, not `adversary`; the Pakistani side (Munir's army, the Saudi pact, Chinese kit) reads India as the existential threat, which is why the pair is asymmetric in feeling but not in grade. Mediation is refused (Kashmir is bilateral; India denies the US brokered the ceasefire). Bond - grievance: partition, four wars, Kashmir. Confidence B because the grade is our structural reading of sources that describe the pair as rivals and India's own posture as deterrence.

IND.note: A partner whose year was a stress test. The 2025 US tariffs reached 50% in Aug 2025 (25% 'reciprocal' plus 25% for buying Russian oil) and put ties 'at their lowest in nearly two decades' (Tribune); the 100,000-dollar H-1B fee (19 Sep 2025) hit the pipeline of Indian engineers (Indians were 71% of 2024 approvals). Repair followed: the 10-year Framework for the US-India Major Defence Partnership signed in Kuala Lumpur on 31 Oct 2025, the 2 Feb 2026 deal cutting the rate to 18% in exchange for restricting Russian oil and buying more American goods, the Quad foreign ministers in New Delhi on 26 May 2026. But the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs on 20 Feb 2026, the first-phase trade agreement is still unsigned (Goyal in June: '99 percent' settled), the Quad leaders' summit India was to host has no date, and on 17 Sep 2026 Congress passed an act authorising tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian energy, to which the MEA answered it will 'take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests'. Net direction: neither warming nor cooling, with the US pulling harder on Russian oil than at any time since 2022. Not an ally: no treaty, no basing, India refuses mediation on Pakistan and keeps Russia. Bond - affinity: diaspora, technology, shared China concern.

IRN.note: Graded adversary, not rival, and this is the least comfortable grade of the card. Against: Hegseth said the operation was not 'a so-called regime-change war', Trump moved to missiles, navy and the bomb, Vance asks for a 'meaningful' cut in enrichment, and the two presidents signed the Pakistan-brokered memorandum of 17 Jun. The atlas reads it as a war between two states each of which would accept the other's defeat, with talks as an instrument of the war, not a thaw. If a settlement on enrichment and Hormuz holds, the right grade becomes rival. Bond - grievance since the 1979 embassy seizure, and now the dead leader.

ISR.note: Ally by stable de facto alignment, not by treaty: the 2016 MOU (USD 38bn to 2028), 68% of Israel's arms imports in 2021-25 (SIPRI), the war on Iran fought together from 28 Feb 2026 ('Netanyahu's war alliance with Trump', Reuters), and a USD 25.8bn emergency arms package in May 2026. Friction is real and public - Trump rebuked the Lebanon campaign and signed an Iran memorandum in June that Israeli ministers say does not bind Israel; Gallup (Feb 2026) found more Americans sympathising with Palestinians than with Israelis; talks on the MOU's successor opened on 5 Jun 2026 with Netanyahu himself backing a phase-out of direct aid - but no Israeli source questions the commitment, so not `reluctant_ally`. Stable: leader-level friction and a shrinking aid frame are offset by deeper military integration. Bond - affinity: shared politics and a large diaspora; no listed bond fits better. The United States has no card of its own, so its grade of Israel is not yet written.

ISR.note: Mortal enemies in the ontology's reference sense, and mutual (mirror of Iran's own reading). Israel's declared aim on 28 Feb 2026 was to remove 'the existential threat posed by the terrorist regime in Iran' and to create the conditions for Iranians to topple it (Netanyahu, 28 Feb and 12 Mar); the strikes killed Ali Khamenei; Iran answers with missile fire on Israeli cities and the pledge of vengeance 'until fully achieved'. Not a bargain between states: Tehran's UN proposal of late September makes an end to Israel's Lebanon offensive a condition, and Washington's own aim (a cut in enrichment, a deal) is narrower than Israel's, so Israel stays the party that wants the regime changed. The war is in its eighth month. Confidence B: Iran's side of the aim is the weaker half of the proof (see Iran's card). Bond - grievance.

Hezbollah's manifestos (1985, 2009) call for the destruction of the Israeli state and it calls the 26 Jun 2026 framework null and void. The Lebanese state is graded separately (rival): the mortal enemy in this triangle is the armed movement, not Beirut. Bond - grievance.

The ceasefire of 10 Oct 2025 changed the structure less than the headlines: about 1,400-1,500 Palestinians killed in its first year, Israel holding about 60% of the Strip, a Hamas disarmament deal announced on 30 Jul 2026 that Hamas accepts only as a 'full package' and Israel has not endorsed. Hamas does not recognise Israel and describes a 1967-lines state as a stage. Bond - grievance.

The Palestinian Authority still sits inside the Oslo security and customs architecture that Israel runs (it collects, and since May 2025 withholds, the clearance revenue that is two-thirds of the PA's budget), so Israel does not seek to destroy the PA the way it seeks to destroy Hamas; but its government rejects a Palestinian state, the E1 tenders, USD 431m for 34 new settlements and the first Area A land seizure advance de facto annexation, and, per PISM, a coalition aim is to block statehood and, if the far right wins, to dismantle the PA. The adversary on the Palestinian side is Hamas, graded separately. Cooling: the election of 27 Oct 2026 offers no contender for prime minister who accepts a state. No source uses the word 'rival'; our reading of the structure (confidence C). Bond - grievance.

Partner, not ally: a bilateral security cooperation agreement (Kyiv, 24 Feb 2024) extending the G7 Vilnius declaration, the host of the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Rome (10-11 July 2025, over EUR 10bn pledged), military aid by decree through the Copasir committee, and support for sanctions and for the EU loan. KAZ.note: Aligned by treaty and by debt, with visible friction. Both sides use the word: the Moscow declaration of 12 Nov 2025 raised ties to 'comprehensive strategic partnership and alliance' and Tokayev hailed 'allied relations' again with Putin in Astana on 28 May 2026 (CSTO and EAEU co-members; the dataset floor would be plain 'ally'). The friction is on the record: Astana refused to recognise the Donetsk and Luhansk 'republics' in Putin's presence (June 2022), calls itself 'not a mediator' on Ukraine, and the Kremlin's levers are the CPC (80% of oil exports), the reported halt of Druzhba transit to Germany from 1 May 2026 and Russian television's attacks of 2022. The 2022 CSTO intervention is the debt that explains the instalments of loyalty (the declaration, the Rosatom plant). Trend stable rather than cooling or warming: the formal ties thickened in 2025-26 while the hedge toward Washington and Beijing thickened at the same time. KOR.note: The ontology's test is whether Seoul's declared aim is the other's defeat or disappearance, and it is not: the Lee government's line is that Seoul respects the North's system, seeks no unification by absorption and commits no hostile acts (Unification Ministry, per PISM), has silenced the loudspeakers, expressed official regret for civilian drone flights, and proposed talks to formally end the war (15 Aug 2026). The hostility is real but it is on Pyongyang's side: Kim's 'hostile states' doctrine (Dec 2023), the Ninth Party Congress (Feb 2026), a border being fortified and crossed (about 20 MDL crossings in August, 30 in September, mines south of the line, a blast on 21 Sep that hurt three soldiers). Even Pyongyang's March 2026 constitution avoids calling the South an enemy by name (38 North), so 'adversary' would claim a mortal enmity that neither side's written aims state. 'Rival', then, with the trend cooling because the other side keeps closing doors. No source uses the word 'rival': the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C), like Kosovo's toward Serbia. Bond - kin: one nation divided, which is why the pair is a feud (kin plus rival) in the faults grid.

LTU.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded from adversary to rival for consistency with Estonia, Latvia-to-be and Poland; 'adversary' is reserved for actors seeking each other's destruction (Iran-Israel), while Lithuania seeks deterrence and a Russian defeat in Ukraine, not the end of the Russian state. The Seimas 'terrorist state' resolutions are the hardest rhetoric in NATO but the structural position is the same as its Baltic neighbours'. Reserved for mortal enemies, and the evidence is a declared view of Russia's regime, not rhetoric: the Seimas voted in May 2022 that Russia supports and perpetrates terrorism, and in March 2023 asked the world to recognise it as a terrorist state; the 2026 national threat assessment treats Russia as the primary threat and dates a limited Baltic war to 3-5 years after a Ukraine ceasefire. Hostile action is documented on Lithuanian soil (IKEA arson sentenced Nov 2025, 36 GPS-spoofing antennas in Kaliningrad). Lithuania does not seek Russia's disappearance, which is why this is the edge of the grade; the Russian regime's behaviour is the problem, and it backs Ukraine's victory by law (0.25% of GDP). Cooling: 'cooling' here means hardening. Residual commerce (Kaliningrad gas transit to 2030) is a legal obligation, not a bond. Bond - grievance: the 1940-91 occupation. The reciprocal Russian stance has not been written.

LTU.note: Mirror of Belarus's own stance toward Lithuania, with the same evidence. Lithuania hosted Tsikhanouskaya's office from 2020 (it moved to Warsaw in Feb 2026), banned Belarusian potash transit via Klaipeda in 2022 and refuses to reopen it while EU sanctions stand (Budrys, Dec 2025 and May 2026), closed its last two crossings on 27 Oct-20 Nov 2025 over the balloons, blocks Astravets power, and the Sinkevicius programme (Jul 2026) keeps isolating Minsk. Rival and not adversary: the aim is pressure and isolation, not the end of the regime, Vilnius is divided on easing (47/46 in an LRT poll cited by Belarus's card), and Washington is pressing for transit and a deputy-minister contact. Trend stable: Lithuania holds while the US softens. No source uses the word 'rival': our reading (confidence C). Bond - grievance: sanctions, the exile base and the seized trucks. Belarus's own card grades Lithuania rival too, so the pair is symmetric.

LTU.note: Co-member of NATO with a visible friction, so the ontology's rule applies: reluctant_ally, not ally. Vilnius wants more American presence than Washington offers: the armoured battalion of about 1,000 left in June 2026 with the next rotation 'under review' (first gap since 2020), a new rotation of up to 1,000 is due in late October, and on 6 Oct 2026 the PM offered to pay for a permanent base while Trump said 'we will certainly look at it'. Against that: US sanctions on Belarusian potash lifted in March 2026 and Washington pressing Lithuania to reopen transit, and Trump's diesel deal with Putin (9 Oct 2026), which Lithuania said weakens the Western position. Lithuania does not hedge: no alternative patron, hence stable and not cooling. No source uses the exact word 'reluctant': our reading (confidence C). Bond - affinity: non-recognition of the 1940 annexation and the pro-American public.

LVA.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded from adversary to rival for consistency with Estonia and Lithuania; 'adversary' is reserved for actors seeking each other's destruction (Iran-Israel). The Saeima's 'state sponsor of terrorism' declaration and the chargé-level relations are the hardest posture in NATO, but Riga's aim is deterrence and a Russian defeat in Ukraine, not the end of the Russian state. The Latvian state itself uses the vocabulary of the mortal enemy: the State Security Service (VDD) puts Russia's services at the head of the threats to the state and a secondary account of its February 2026 report calls Russia an existential threat; the Saeima declared Russia a state sponsor of terrorism on 11 Aug 2022 (67 votes, none against); relations were cut to charge d'affaires level on 24 Feb 2023; and Latvian soil has seen Russian-directed arson cells (cases of 2023-25), GPS jamming from Kaliningrad, and Russian rail crossings shut from 1 Jul 2026. Adversary rather than rival because the declared Latvian aim is Russia's defeat in Ukraine and the Russian state is named the threat to Latvia's existence, not a competitor. The case against: Riga seeks no change of regime in Moscow, keeps an embassy, and still sold EUR 962.5m of goods to Russia in 2025 (4.9% of exports), so the grade is the harder of two readings (the 'rival' reading is the fallback). Bond - grievance: the 1940 occupation and the Soviet deportations, and more than a third of residents who are not ethnic Latvians, mostly Russian-speaking.

MAR.note: Read from Rabat: the rupture was Algiers' act (24 Aug 2021, 'hostile actions'; airspace closed 22 Sep, gas contract lapsed 31 Oct, visas on Moroccans 26 Sep 2024), the border has been shut since 1994, and the Sahara file names Algeria among the parties although it did not vote on Resolution 2797. Rabat's declared line is not Algeria's defeat but normal relations (the king repeated his offer on 30 Jul 2022), so the ontology's mortal 'adversary' does not fit; Carnegie speaks of a 'rivalry' extending into the Sahel and CFR of Algerian hostility toward Morocco. Algeria spends four times as much on arms (USD 21.8bn against 5.5bn, SIPRI 2024). Bond - kin: shared language, faith and history, the 'brotherly peoples' of the royal speeches; kin plus rival is the textbook feud. Trend stable: no thaw (visa regime 2024, the April 2025 hack blamed on Algerian hackers), no new rupture.

Mexico invited Putin to her inauguration like every state it has relations with, which drew criticism because Mexico is a party to the Rome Statute; Putin did not attend and sent an envoy (Zeta Tijuana). A US State Department report on alleged Russian intelligence officers posing as diplomats in Mexico, which Sheinbaum downplayed while asking for a report (Posta, undated), is the only friction seen and is not graded. No 2026 source on Russia and Mexico was found. Bond none. Confidence C: 2024 sources, a posture read from them.

MEX.note: Neutral, cooling: friction short of a break. In Oct 2025 Sheinbaum demanded the immediate release and repatriation of six Mexicans held at Ashdod after the Gaza-bound flotilla, and the foreign ministry sent four diplomatic notes (Zeta Tijuana, Telemundo); Israel's foreign minister called the flotilla a provocation linked to Hamas. In Apr-May 2026 the foreign ministry again moved to protect Mexicans on the Global Sumud Flotilla intercepted off Crete with 177 detained, one Mexican back on 2 May, and demanded consular access and respect for their integrity (Anadolu Agency). Sheinbaum has called the killing in Gaza a genocide and backs a two-state solution (Por Esto, N+). Israel was one of seven countries that voted against the UN resolution Mexico supported on the Cuba embargo (UN DPPA). Neutral not rival: relations are not suspended, no sanction is read and the quarrel is about consular treatment and rhetoric. Bond none. Gap: ambassadors, trade, any 2026 Israeli statement about Mexico; the ISR card holds no stance toward Mexico yet.

MKD.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). Bulgaria is the first obstacle on Skopje's EU path: it has blocked the opening of negotiations since 2020 and, with the 2022 French proposal, requires the constitution to name Bulgarians (Zhelyazkov, Oct 2025: Sofia adds no new condition to the 2022 proposal). Skopje answers with two conditions (rights for Macedonians in Bulgaria; no further bilateral vetoes) and the Commission notes that no steps have been taken. Incidents keep the wound open: the Ivan Mihailov club sentence (Jun 2025), the arson of two Bulgarian embassy cars in Skopje (15 Jun 2026, suspect detained, motive unknown). The grade is rival, not ally, although both are NATO members (the dataset would derive 'ally'): Sofia's claim that Macedonian language and history are Bulgarian is a contest over identity, and the bilateral friendship treaty of 2017 and Corridor 8 are working in parallel. Trend stable: von der Leyen's visit of 2 Oct 2026 produced a first step, but no movement on the constitution. Bond - grievance: history, language, the 1943 Vatasha anniversary a day after the arson.

MKD.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). Prespa Agreement in force since February 2019; Greece is a NATO co-member, a major investor and the partner of the Gevgelija-Negotino gas interconnector and the Markova Noga-Lemos border crossing (Commission: cooperation 'intensified'). But Athens holds the other veto: it accuses Mickoski and President Siljanovska-Davkova of 'flagrant violation' by using 'Macedonia' in domestic contexts, says it will not ratify three cooperation memoranda until Skopje complies, and the government spokesman again tied the EU road to Greece in early October 2026. Partner rather than ally despite common NATO membership (the dataset would derive 'ally'): the name is a standing grievance and Mickoski treats Prespa as a mistake he will not repeat. Not rival, because the cooperation on energy and borders is real and Skopje asks for 'unconditional' Greek support. Trend cooling: 2024-26 friction, nothing resolved.

MKD.note: Albania is the motherland of North Macedonia's large ethnic Albanian community, and a NATO co-member (the dataset would derive 'ally'). The Commission says relations 'remained good' with agreements on security, defence, infrastructure and energy, and a 400 kV interconnector line is under implementation. Partner, not ally: no bilateral alliance, and the Mickoski government has a recurring friction with Tirana-adjacent politics - students and politicians from Albania and Kosovo joined the April-May 2026 bar-exam protests, DUI's Trajanov called that 'impermissible external influence', and Albania left the cross-border programme without a Joint Technical Secretariat in July 2024 (Commission). MMR.note: Patron, not partner and not quite ally. Beijing endorsed the Dec 2025-Jan 2026 election, Wang Yi was the first senior Chinese political visitor to the new president (Naypyidaw, 25 Apr 2026), Min Aung Hlaing went to China in June and the joint statement of 17 Jun 2026 speeds up Kyaukphyu, the CMEC railway and the oil and gas pipelines, adds a BRI plan and a yuan-kyat settlement, and Myanmar reaffirmed One China. Not 'ally': there is no treaty, and the alignment is by necessity with visible friction - Beijing broke the northern alliance by blockading and detaining MNDAA leaders until Lashio came back (22 Apr 2025), keeps its own channel to the KIA (the rare-earth belt) and joined the Thai-Myanmar scam-centre crackdown it had pressed for. Luttwak reading: the junta survives by being useful to its patron against its own people, and the patron's calculus is a quiet border, open pipelines and no Western-aligned Naypyidaw, not a junta victory.
